facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this feeling worsened in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Promotion at school
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years. She was asked to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and I have loved it and then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being inadequate
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety symptoms on Sunday evenings
facts.content: On Sunday evenings, Hannah's chest gets tight and she rehearses Monday's staff meeting in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what others might think of her if she gets it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say, then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being incompetent
facts.content: Hannah fears people will think she is out of her depth or that she can't read.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Rewriting email to governors
facts.content: Last week, Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of Mr. Hargraves' opinion
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding the behavior policy email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Feeling of inauthenticity
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable.
facts.evidence: I feel like I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Feeling like a child
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother's past career
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother's career
facts.content: Hannah constantly compares her own work to what her mother might have done.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's supportive advice
facts.content: Hannah's mother tells her she worries too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Waking up early
facts.content: Hannah wakes up at 4 every morning to go through her to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at 4 every morning.

facts.heading: Caffeine intake for energy
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six, then I can't sit still in the afternoons.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: In the afternoons, Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's perspective
facts.content: Hannah's partner, Ben, thinks if something is a problem, it should be fixed.
facts.evidence: He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.

facts.heading: Loss of school friendships
facts.content: Hannah no longer eats lunch with her former classmates because she is now their line manager.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Missing teaching aspect
facts.content: Hannah misses the daily experience of a child learning something new.
facts.evidence: The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Regret about accepting promotion
facts.content: Hannah cried after accepting the promotion because she felt she couldn't say no to her superior.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Fear of going back to past
facts.content: Hannah feels fear regarding going back to a past situation.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Lack of validation from others
facts.content: Hannah feels that people only say 'well done' to her.
facts.evidence: Nobody has asked me that, they just say well done.

facts.heading: Relaxed during summer holidays
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays while walking in the lakes.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Support during holidays
facts.content: Hannah felt supported during the summer holidays when walking in the lakes.
facts.evidence: Ben carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Worsening before term
facts.content: Hannah felt like a wreck the week before term started.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again.

facts.heading: Eating difficulties before term
facts.content: Hannah could not eat on the Sunday before term started.
facts.evidence: I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Coping habit: evening writing
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening.

facts.heading: Stopped writing down positives
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing down positive things because she felt silly.
facts.evidence: I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Feeling of bragging
facts.content: Hannah felt like she was bragging to herself in a notebook.
facts.evidence: As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook.

facts.heading: Goal: work without feeling fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do her job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal: meeting behavior

facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first.

facts.heading: Goal: email frequency

facts.evidence: Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal: evening comfort

facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling lighter after stating goals

facts.evidence: Lighter.

facts.heading: Feeling tearful after stating goals

facts.evidence: A bit tearful actually.

facts.evidence: He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps?

facts.evidence: I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget.
